source.title: When 20 Agents Fail to Sort: The Distributed Sorting Benchmark for Scalable Multi-Agent Systems

assessments.primary_source_quality: Very strong: peer-reviewed Findings ACL paper, deterministic collective-correctness benchmark, three models, three communication backends, scaling over agent counts/input structure, repeated experimental settings, component ablations, explicit statistical regression diagnostic, and additional loose/medium coupling tasks without task-specific tuning.
assessments.quantitative_result: On Shared K-V, CAMOC raises success from 38.2%→84.7% for DeepSeek-V3.1, 33.7%→67.2% for Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, and 25.6%→56.5% for GPT-OSS-120B. The paper reports success gains up to 40 percentage points overall. Message/submission ablations show distinct contributions; under Shared K-V, removing structured messaging reduces DeepSeek success 84.7%→70.6% and GPT-OSS 56.5%→52.1%. The mechanism also transfers without task-specific tuning to Distributed Maximum (~58%→~71%) and Prefix Sum (~32%→~43%) for DeepSeek-V3.1. One exception is statistically significant: Qwen3 P2P falls from Base 56.9% to CAMOC 51.2% (p<0.05), with the paper attributing the regression to One-shot Commitment suppressing useful iterative refinement.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong. Base, full CAMOC and component ablations are compared within the same model/backend/task settings, with deterministic task correctness and token/round/communication metrics. The exception analysis prevents interpreting the bundle as uniformly beneficial.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for structured coordination messaging and explicit submission/termination control in tightly coupled distributed tasks. Global-metadata/one-shot components are part of a bundle, and one-shot commitment has a demonstrated backend/model regression, so the transferable causal claim should be component-specific and adaptive rather than 'always use CAMOC'.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: ACL full text reports code/data availability and formal orchestration details; comparator directly verified the primary paper tables/pages for the headline effects and regression.
assessments.external_replication: No separate independent replication identified, but results span multiple models, backends and additional coupling tasks with explicit ablations.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong evidence that naive agent-count scaling degrades correctness/efficiency on tightly coupled state, and that one-shot suppression of refinement can itself harm some model/backend settings.
scope_limits: Distributed sorting/maximum/prefix-sum are algorithmic coordination tasks with exact ground truth, not open-ended research collaboration.
CAMOC benefits are largest under weak/brittle shared-state coordination; not every backend benefits from every component.
One-shot commitment must remain adaptive because Qwen3 P2P significantly regressed.
The paper validates protocol engineering for coupled outputs, not a claim that communication improves independent discovery.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A- for structured coordination plus verification in the tested tightly coupled distributed tasks, with a required exception for one-shot commitment.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- for applying early shared metadata/single-authoritative commit to O or its external workers until matched coupled-output tasks show net benefit and model/backend-specific refinement needs are measured.

source.title: SILO-BENCH: A Scalable Environment for Evaluating Distributed Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

assessments.primary_source_quality: Very strong diagnostic evidence: ACL long paper, 30 algorithmic tasks across three communication-complexity levels, three frontier LLMs, three protocols, six agent scales, 54 configurations and 1,620 experiments with exact correctness and communication/efficiency metrics. Code is explicitly linked in the paper.
assessments.quantitative_result: Success declines sharply with agent count: DeepSeek-V3.1 averages 61.2% at N=2 and 18.1% at N=100; GPT-OSS-120B 34.4%→6.4%; Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B 17.2%→1.3%. The full paper reports DeepSeek difficulty averages of 62.0% Level I, 35.1% Level II and 11.7% Level III. Under high coordination complexity, scaling can eliminate success entirely at large N. The source attributes failure to a Communication-Reasoning Gap: agents often obtain/exchange enough information but fail to synthesize distributed state into the correct global output.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for the scaling phenomenon: agent count, protocol, model and coordination-complexity level are systematically varied under exact ground truth. It is a benchmark/diagnostic study, not a treatment trial of deterministic recombination or small authoritative aggregation.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for agent-count × coordination-complexity interaction and poor free-form distributed synthesis. Weak for the worker's proposed remedy of moving recombination into deterministic machinery/small aggregators, which is an inference from the diagnosed failure rather than a tested SILO-BENCH intervention.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Primary ACL PDF links public code and fully specifies benchmark dimensions; comparator directly verified the source and exact agent-scale table.
assessments.external_replication: MAS-BENCH independently provides conceptually aligned evidence that tightly coupled coordination degrades with N, but task/protocol designs differ, so treat it as corroboration rather than replication of exact scaling curves.
assessments.failure_evidence: Very strong within exact distributed computation: active communication and apparently sensible topology discovery do not imply correct global synthesis, and more agents can compound the coordination tax.
scope_limits: Algorithmic information-silo tasks, not independent candidate search or loosely coupled parallel work.
The result is evidence against naive large-N coupled free-form computation, not against large-N independent evaluator-gated search.
Exact N thresholds are model/task/protocol-specific and should not be copied into O.
Deterministic recombination is a plausible remedy but is not directly tested by this paper.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A- for the existence and severity of coordination-scaling tax in the SILO-BENCH settings.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C for deterministic/small-authority recombination as a remedy until compared against conversational recombination on matched O/external-research coupled tasks.

assessments.primary_source_quality: Built from two strong peer-reviewed coordination studies plus the worker's earlier matched-compute reasoning evidence, but the adaptive controller itself is not evaluated in this record.
assessments.quantitative_result: Both sources show that marginal value of added agents depends strongly on task coupling, model/backend and protocol, including outright regressions for some components and near-zero success at high coordination complexity/large N.
assessments.matched_baseline: No direct learned/adaptive-N controller comparison in the assessed record.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong evidence that a fixed maximize-N rule is invalid; weak evidence for any particular online controller mapping difficulty/coupling/novelty/cost to N/topology.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Underlying benchmark artifacts are available; controller hypothesis has no artifact because it is not yet a tested system.
assessments.external_replication: The two peer-reviewed sources independently support context-dependent coordination scaling.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong against fixed large-N coupled collaboration and against treating communication volume as progress.
scope_limits: Controller inputs and optimization objective are proposed, not validated.
Independent discovery and coupled computation have different scaling regimes and should not share one policy without explicit task classification.
Marginal novelty/evidence yield needs its own measurement for research workers.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A- for the premise that optimal N/protocol is context dependent in the tested coordination tasks.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C for an adaptive controller until a matched online allocation experiment demonstrates better outcome/compute tradeoffs.

cross_source_synthesis: The peer-reviewed multi-agent evidence supports a sharp distinction between independent search and coupled shared-state computation. The assessed failures concern the latter and should not be generalized to isolated research-worker breadth.

Protocol design can recover much of the lost correctness in tightly coupled tasks, but component-level effects are model/backend dependent; one-shot commitment is specifically falsified as universally beneficial.

Large-N coordination failure is now supported by two separate ACL 2026 benchmarks with different task formulations. This is strong failure evidence for naive conversational distributed computation, but the deterministic-aggregator remedy still needs a direct experiment.
An adaptive N/topology policy is evidence-motivated but not evidence-established.
